summary: Chicago socialite Elizabeth Dilling became a leading American red-baiter in the 1930s with The Red Network, campaigned with Father Coughlin against FDR, spread antisemitic conspiracy theories, praised Nazi Germany and was tried for sedition.
keywords: Red Revolution: Do We Want It Here?

evidence.note: Birth in Chicago in 1894 and family background
1931 trip to Moscow and Leningrad that set off her anti-communist crusade
Works with Harry Jung, early US distributor of the Protocols; Paul Reveres bar Jews
Long segment on Father Coughlin's life and radio career as her idol
1936 campaign against FDR, sabotage of Borah, attempts to help Landon
Attends the 1938 Nuremberg Rally and speaks at German American Bund events
Host reads Klan and antisemitic Aryan Bookstore propaganda at length
Sedition charge in 1942, trial, dismissal in 1946

notes: Transcript calls the Vigilant Intelligence Federation director Harry Young; he is usually spelled Harry Jung. Germany visit (1938 Nuremberg Rally) is brief, so DE left out of setting. Glenn Beck and modern neo-Nazi citations are a short aside, so reaches_present is false. Primary theme fascism-far-right since she is an American fascist; nazism kept secondary for her open Nazi sympathies.
